analysis.title: Situation Room: Into bonds and stocks
key_insights: US HG bond fund and ETF inflows were +$7.70bn in the week ending Nov 4, up from +$4.35bn the prior week. HG Funds took in +$1.59bn (the biggest inflow in 9 weeks, from -$2.85bn), while HG ETF inflows slowed to +$6.11bn from +$7.20bn.
The HG fund inflow was helped by the large first-of-month fund inflows. Excluding the first-day fund flow, the weekly HG inflow was +$5.0bn, similar to the prior week.
Short-term HG inflows rose to +$1.29bn from +$0.30bn, and ex-short-term HG inflows rose to +$6.40bn from +$4.05bn.
Equity fund inflows improved to +$29.54bn from +$14.54bn in the prior week. Loan fund flows turned to a +$0.13bn inflow from -$0.31bn.
HY flows were roughly steady at +$1.55bn (vs +$1.80bn). Muni inflows slowed to +$1.61bn from +$2.60bn, and global EM bond funds saw outflows of -$0.47bn (vs -$0.44bn).
Money market funds reported a +$94.46bn inflow in the week, after an -$11.36bn outflow the week before.

YTD fund flows as of Nov 4: HG +8.2% of AUM ($416.3bn), HY +1.6% ($7.4bn), loans +9.1% ($16.2bn), EM +2.9% ($25.9bn), munis +8.4% ($92.1bn), all fixed income +8.6% ($717.3bn), money markets +2.7% ($225.8bn), equities +1.5% ($430.8bn). Loans have had the biggest YTD inflows as a share of AUM, followed by munis.

US IG issuance was $22bn across 11 deals on Nov 5, $74.9bn week-to-date and month-to-date. The average new issue concession was 12.2bps on the day, and this week's new issues are trading 4bps tighter on average from pricing.
Oracle priced a five-tranche IG deal on Nov 2 (3Y $2.0bn at +240, 5Y $1.75bn at +275, 7Y $2.25bn at +305, 10Y $2.5bn at +310, 20Y $1.5bn at +335), rated Baa2/BBB-. Concessions ran 3-18bps.

Meta priced a five-tranche deal on Nov 3 (5Y $3.25bn at +110, 7Y $3.25bn at +145, 10Y $4.0bn at +160, 20Y $1.75bn at +200, 30Y $2.75bn at +220), rated Aa3/AA-. The 5Y and 7Y carried 32bps concessions, and the 30Y carried 5bps.

Apple came to market on Nov 5 with a multi-tranche deal including a 10Y $2.0bn at +55 (38bps concession) and a 7Y $1.25bn at +45 (24bps concession). HCA priced a seven-tranche fixed-rate deal on Nov 2, led by a $1.5bn 10Y at +120.
BofA estimates IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds rose to +$7.2bn on Nov 5 from -$5.0bn on Oct 28. Dealer inventory DV01 rose to -$3.5mn from -$10.5mn.

Estimated net dealer buying in HG was +$389mn on Nov 5, +$10,598mn over one week and +$24,362mn over four weeks. By sector over four weeks, Banks/Brokers +$6,976mn, Health Care +$4,108mn, Technology +$3,401mn, and Utilities +$2,724mn. Utilities saw net dealer selling of $316mn on Nov 5.
Daily HG fund inflow was $1,000mn on Nov 4, vs -$1,270mn on Nov 3. Average daily HG inflow was $598mn in November so far, vs $708mn in October.
BofA notes HG fund flows tend to follow returns, but have been decoupled from returns since around Oct 2024.

vol_and_positioning: Weekly equity fund inflows of +$29.54bn were roughly double the prior week's +$14.54bn.
Money market funds took in +$94.46bn in the week ending Nov 4, after an -$11.36bn outflow the prior week.
Net foreign buying proxy for 10yr+ IG: the 12-day moving average of foreign buying rose by $14mn over the five business days ending Nov 5, while the 30-year Treasury yield changed by 0bps.
